$comment: Template for a Tribe-lane OpenCode session (change configure-phi-lanes). NOT loaded automatically: OpenCode reads .opencode/opencode.json / opencode.jsonc. Copy this to that path (or merge it into your own, gitignored copy) before use. Every value below is a TRIBE_MODEL_* environment variable reference via OpenCode's {env:VAR} substitution (verify this syntax against your installed OpenCode version); never commit a copy with a real endpoint, model name or key, per ATH-D-001 and the phi-lane-policy skill.
$denyNote: Deny off-lane channels (task 4.1, carried from the define-portable-team-manifest security review): the permission.webfetch key above denies OpenCode's own web-fetch tool. OpenCode auto-loads only this repo's own .opencode/plugins/fhir-guards.js (the guard/ledger/phi-lane hooks); there is no separate 'disable other plugins' setting to add here because none are referenced. Verify the exact permission key against your installed OpenCode version before relying on it.
$laneNote: phi-lane-guard (.claude/hooks/src/phi-lane-guard.mts) proves the lane from the process environment, not from this file. Before launching OpenCode with this provider active, export in your shell (never in a committed file): PHI_LANE=tribe, TRIBE_MODEL_BASE_URL, TRIBE_MODEL_API_KEY, TRIBE_MODEL_NAME, and AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL set to the same value as TRIBE_MODEL_BASE_URL. Declaring PHI_LANE=tribe without a matching AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL is still the synthetic lane (phi-lane-policy): the guard denies non-sandbox FHIR pulls either way. Never export these variables for a cloud/non-Tribe model.
